First, I usually pick up coffee for my co-worker every morning. It's a small gesture, but it shows that I care about their well-being and want to make their day a bit easier. It's a routine that we've established, and I think they appreciate it. But this morning, my co-worker is out of town. So, I didn't pick up their coffee. Another angle is the effort involved. Picking up coffee every morning takes a bit of time and money. If my co-worker isn't there, it's reasonable to skip it to save those resources. But if I usually do it as a favor, stopping might feel like I'm not holding up my end of the arrangement. I'm also thinking about the relationship aspect. If I consistently pick up coffee for them, stopping once might not be a big deal. But if it's a regular thing, maybe I should communicate that I won't be doing it today because they're away. It's more about the intention and communication. If I had communicated that I wouldn't be getting it because they're out, that would be considerate. If I just stopped without any reason, it might seem like I'm being inconsiderate. So, considering all these factors, I think it's more about the context and communication rather than the action itself being right or wrong. If I had communicated, it would be better. Since I didn't, maybe it's a bit inconsiderate, but not necessarily wrong.
